title: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)

sections.label: COVID-19 support spending total
sections.summary: The Government spent close to $100 billion, almost 20% of GDP, in economic, social and public health measures over FY2020 and FY2021 Budgets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Over a series of Budgets in FY2020 and FY2021, the Government had spent close to $100 billion, or almost 20% of GDP, in economic and social support as well as public health management measures.

sections.label: Global fiscal pandemic responses
sections.summary: Governments worldwide mobilised massive fiscal policy responses totalling US$14 trillion at end-2020 to cope with COVID-19's health and economic consequences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, to cope with the health and economic consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic, governments around the world had mobilised massive fiscal policy responses totalling US$14 trillion at end-2020.

sections.label: COVID-19 support programme fraud
sections.summary: The UK, US and Singapore dealt with fraud and error in COVID-19 support programmes, including 57 Singapore reports involving some $1.7 million of grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Most recently, the UK government had come under scrutiny for fraud and error in the country’s COVID-19 support programmes, which are expected to cost the British taxpayers over £15 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Similarly, in the US, fraud or improper payments are likely to account for more than US$90 billion of the government’s emergency pandemic aid for the unemployed and small businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Here, in Singapore, we have had also to deal with 57 reports of fraud involving some $1.7 million of COVID-19 grants.

sections.label: Request for COVID-19 spending breakdown
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to present the $100 billion COVID-19 spending in Budget format with breakdown by category and Ministry, and explain $5 billion annual R&D spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister present the $100 billion COVID-19 spending in the same format as the Budget, with detailed breakdown by spending category and by Ministry and explain where is the $5 billion annual spending on R&D?

sections.label: Government financial assets and returns
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to confirm $1.4 trillion total financial assets as at 31 March 2021, MAS reserves and over $40 billion yearly net investment returns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister confirm that the Government has reported total financial assets of $1.4 trillion as at 31 March 2021 and that MAS has accumulated close to $200 billion of new reserves in the last two years and all these financial assets are now producing more than $40 billion in net investment returns per year?

sections.label: Multi-tiered GST additional cost
sections.summary: The Finance Minister said additional cost would be incurred for having multi-tiered GST.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Finance Minister said that additional cost would be incurred for having multi-tiered GST.

sections.label: Corporate tax versus GST revenue
sections.summary: Asks the Finance Minister how much the effective corporate tax rate would need to rise to match a 2% GST hike.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can the Finance Minister also share with us how much the effective corporate tax rate would have to be raised by to generate the same revenue as a 2% hike in GST?

sections.label: HDB buying land from SLA
sections.summary: Seeks confirmation that under the current arrangement, land bought cheaply by the Government is sold repeatedly to HDB at prevailing land price.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, can I seek confirmation from the Finance Minister that under the current arrangement of HDB buying land from SLA, that the same piece of land acquired at low cost by the Government in the past will be sold repeatedly to HDB at the prevailing land price?

sections.label: Drivers facing fuel price revisions
sections.summary: Notes that while attention is on fuel prices rising from the Ukraine war, drivers faced at least 18 fuel price revisions in 14 months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While all eyes are fixed on the recent escalating fuel prices caused by the war in Ukraine, our drivers have been standing stoic in facing fuel price revisions of at least 18 times in the past 14 months.

sections.label: Borrowing for infrastructure developments
sections.summary: Recalls the Prime Minister's words and a Bill passed last year allowing up to $90 billion of infrastructure developments through borrowing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: Yet, as the Prime Minister said, “We will never be done building Singapore.” Members will remember that we passed a Bill in Parliament last year that allows the Government to undertake up to $90 billion of infrastructure developments through borrowing.

sections.label: Governance framework for infrastructure projects
sections.summary: Cites a Project Management Institute report on poor project management costs and asks what governance framework manages risks for upcoming infrastructure projects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: A report by the Project Management Institute estimates that poor project management costs an average of 12.7% of total budgets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: If applied to the $90 billion of infrastructure projects in the pipeline, we could potentially waste $11.4 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: Their checks revealed lapses in adjustments for price fluctuations, a lack of assurance in quantities used for projects, and weaknesses in management of contract variations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Minister what governance framework is in place to manage the risks associated with the upcoming infrastructure projects, including supply chain disruptions, in the post-COVID-19 era?

sections.label: Government support for suppliers
sections.summary: Asks how the Government, as a major buyer, has supported suppliers beyond earlier invoice payment, especially local SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As a major buyer of goods and services itself, how has the Government supported its suppliers during this challenging period?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Beyond attempting to settle the supplier’s invoice earlier than what payment terms provide for, how has the Government exercised flexibility and demonstrated solidarity with its suppliers, especially local SMEs?

sections.label: MOF green business initiatives
sections.summary: MOF and its agencies drive initiatives to help businesses, especially SMEs, innovate and build capabilities for green opportunities and skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What initiatives are MOF and its agencies driving to enhance Singapore's business ecosystem to help our businesses, especially SMEs, innovate, access and build the capabilities to participate in these new green opportunities and skills?

sections.label: MOF business process efficiency measures
sections.summary: MOF initiated measures or programmes to continuously improve the efficiency of business processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: As such, what are some of the measures or programmes initiated by MOF to ensure that we continuously improve the efficiency of our business processes?

sections.label: Accountability and governance for spending
sections.summary: Governance and monitoring structures were established to ensure accountability for public resources and strengthen programme performance.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Ms Foo Mee Har asked how we strengthen accountability and governance for our spending.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have established governance and monitoring structures to ensure proper accountability for the use of public resources and strengthen performance for programmes.

sections.label: Cases referred to Police
sections.summary: As of last week, 14 cases have been referred to the Police.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As of last week, 14 cases have been referred to the Police.

sections.label: JSS overpayment recovery
sections.summary: Over 99% of the $370 million JSS overpayment has been recovered, with work ongoing on the rest.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Out of the $370 million JSS overpayment discovered earlier, we have recovered over 99% and are working on recovering the rest.

sections.label: MOF project cost savings
sections.summary: Of projects submitted for approval last year, MOF achieved about $600 million in cost savings, 4% of $14.4 billion capital cost.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Of the projects submitted for approval last year, MOF managed to achieve cost savings of about $600 million or 4% of a capital cost of $14.4 billion.

sections.label: Energy usage and substations reduction
sections.summary: This reduces total energy usage and the number of substations required, expected to result in life-cycle cost savings of about $280 million.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This reduces total energy usage and the number of substations required.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This is expected to result in life-cycle cost savings of about $280 million.

sections.label: GST revenue and healthcare spending
sections.summary: At a 9% GST rate, an additional 0.7% of GDP per year is expected, about $3.5 billion, less than projected healthcare spending increases.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: At a GST rate of 9%, we expect to collect an additional 0.7% of GDP per year, currently estimated to be about $3.5 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This is less than the projected increase in healthcare spending, which could amount to over one-percentage point of GDP by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: At the same time, the enhanced permanent GST Voucher scheme will cost about $500 million more per year in FY 2023, compared to today.

sections.label: JSS and RSS disbursement process
sections.summary: Efforts enhanced the JSS and RSS disbursement process, disbursing more than $28 billion of JSS to about 180,000 employers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Beyond providing targeted support, we have invested efforts to enhance the JSS and RSS disbursement process, to make timely payments to employers and eligible tenants and owners.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have disbursed more than $28 billion of JSS to about 180,000 employers expeditiously, with the most recent tranche being disbursed within two months from the announcement of the extended support for businesses most adversely affected by COVID-19 restrictions.

sections.label: Automatic payouts under scheme
sections.summary: More than 110,000 payouts, worth almost $1 billion, were disbursed automatically within two months from the scheme's announcement.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: More than 110,000 payouts, worth almost $1 billion, were disbursed automatically within two months from the announcement of the scheme.

sections.label: Advanced payments for construction contracts
sections.summary: Advanced payments worth $665 million were made for over 450 public sector construction contracts, plus more than $230 million in co-shared costs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: When the pandemic first broke out in 2020, we made advanced payments, worth $665 million, for over 450 public sector construction contracts, to help contractors tide over work stoppages.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We also provided support of more than $230 million by co-sharing costs.

sections.label: JSS impetus and sector exclusions
sections.summary: The initial impetus for schemes like JSS was timely cash flow support for businesses to protect local workers, later excluding well-performing sectors such as supermarkets.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The initial impetus for schemes like JSS was to provide timely cash flow support to businesses to protect our local workers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We then adjusted our approach to exclude those sectors, such as supermarkets, which were doing very well.

sections.label: Retailers food donation drives
sections.summary: DFI Retail Group donated food and healthcare essentials through Cold Storage and Giant, while FairPrice pledged $1.2 million to 600 families over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For example, DFI Retail Group ramped up efforts to donate food and healthcare essentials to the needy through a food donation drive through the group’s grocery stores Cold Storage and Giant, while FairPrice pledged in January 2022 to donate $1.2 million to 600 families over three years to help low-income families cope with higher costs of living.

sections.label: Software developers register onboarding
sections.summary: Since its October 2021 launch, about 30 software developers have onboarded or expressed interest to onboard the register.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Since its launch in October 2021, about 30 software developers have onboarded or expressed interest to onboard the register.

sections.label: Traders e-guarantees with Customs
sections.summary: Close to 200 traders lodged e-guarantees with Customs last year, saving three hours and $30 for each e-guarantee.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Close to 200 traders lodged e-guarantees with Customs last year, saving three hours and $30 for each e-guarantee.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Mark supplier requirement
sections.summary: From March 2023, eligible suppliers must be accredited with the Progressive Wage Mark, extended to retail, food services, waste management and suppliers with in-house workers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Government will require eligible suppliers to be accredited with the Progressive Wage Mark from March 2023, to support our lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Along with the expansion of the Progressive Wage Model, the requirement for suppliers to attain the Progressive Wage Mark will be extended to the retail, food services and waste management sectors, and suppliers with in-house cleaners, security officers, landscape workers, administrators and drivers.

sections.label: GST on water conservation tax
sections.summary: At the future 9% GST, monthly GST on water conservation tax is around 90 cents for 3-room and 4-room HDB households and under 60 cents for one-room and two-room households.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: At the future 9% GST, the amount of GST payable on the water conservation tax each month is around 90 cents for 3-room and 4-room HDB households, on average, and less than 60 cents for one-room and two-room households.

sections.label: U-Save rebates utilities bills
sections.summary: U-Save rebates from the Household Support Package and Assurance Package come up to about eight to 10 months' worth of utilities bills, excluding the permanent GST Voucher scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In fact, when you add the U-Save rebates from the Household Support Package together with the Assurance Package, it will come up to about eight to 10 months' worth of utilities bills, and this is not taking into account the permanent GST Voucher scheme, which also has a U-Save component.

sections.label: GST and lower-income buffers
sections.summary: The Government applies GST to all, including basic essentials, while buffering lower-income and middle-income groups.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Government does not believe that basic essentials should be exempt.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: What we do is we apply GST across the board for everybody, but we ensure that the lower-income are buffered against this and the middle-income also receive a certain amount of benefits, so they get some buffer as well.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance had earlier shown that for every dollar of tax paid, the lower-income get back $4 to the dollar, and the middle-income get back $2 to the dollar.

sections.label: Land as national asset
sections.summary: The Government's fundamental approach treats land as a national asset, like an endowment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Fundamentally, our approach is this: land is a national asset, think of it as an endowment.

sections.label: Budget Book expenditure classification
sections.summary: The Budget Book classifies Government expenditure by Ministries and breaks it down into object classes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In the Budget Book, the Government's expenditure is classified by Ministries and broken down into object classes based on the nature of the spending.

sections.label: COVID-19 spending and financial assets
sections.summary: A Member asks the Government to single out COVID-19 expenditures and confirm financial assets figures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Yes, I think we will refer to the Budget Book again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But I think if the Government can help us by singling out all the COVID-19 expenditures, that will help our understanding better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The second question is, I have specifically asked for confirmation about the financial assets, S$1.4 trillion, which is already a reported number, and also some other figures, S$200 billion new reserves accumulated by MAS.

sections.label: Corporate tax and GST questions
sections.summary: Questions were asked on the corporate tax rate increase needed to match a 2% GST hike and the expected GST rate in 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: One of which is: what would be the corporate tax rate increase that would be necessary to raise the same amount of revenue as a 2% hike in GST?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: And also, what is the expected rate of GST in 2030?

sections.label: GST raised in 2023 and 2024
sections.summary: The GST was raised by two percentage points in 2023 and 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Right now, we have just gone through one exercise of raising the GST by two percentage points in 2023 and 2024.
